Ashara’s tail gives one firm tap against her chair.

“I will. A ranked drill isn’t a lesson for someone who’s never held a blade.”

“The bouts are open tomorrow,” Rashid says. “Watch first. Decide afterward.”

“That’s all I meant.”

A server arrives with pear tart and cream, and the subject passes on. Caelindra turns her attention to Aldric instead.

“Does the chapel bell truly begin before breakfast?”

“It begins at dawn,” Aldric says. “Waking everyone is incidental.”

Thessaly unwraps another sweet. “The distinction does not alter the result.”

Ashara laughs, and even Rashid’s expression eases.

When the last plates are cleared, Rashid rises. “I need to honor an earlier promise.”

“Dawn,” Ashara says.

“Dawn.”

At the dining-hall arch, Dena turns back toward you, her splinted wrist tucked against her dark sleeve.

“Garvey, there’s room for another hand. We’re playing Glass Crows. I’ll explain it once, then I’m not explaining it again.”
